newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Speciality coffees seen reversing U.S. demand fall.
newsitem.headline: Speciality coffees seen reversing U.S. demand fall.

text.p: Clear indications are now emerging in the U.S. that the continued positive growth in the specialty coffee sector is having an impact on overall volume consumption, the head of the International Coffee Organisation (ICO) said.
Executive director Celsius Lodder's remarks were in a speech delivered by the ICO's Robert Hagen at an international coffee seminar in Rio on Tuesday.
Lodder said the success of the speciality sector had led to the prospect of a reversal in the declining trend that has been a characteristic of the U.S. coffee market since the early sixties.

Whereas consumption declined from 21.9 million to 17.5 million 60-kg bags from 1965 to 1995, a growth rate of 1 percent a year from 1995 to 2000 should lead to consumption reaching some 18.4 million bags by the latter year, with the value of the specialty sector exceeding $3 billion.
